clinician.trajectory_summary: A 28-year-old male presented with a 2-month history of nonproductive progressive cough and left flank pain. Physical exam revealed abdominal distention with a palpable large mass in the left upper quadrant. Initial contrast-enhanced CT showed a heterogeneously enhancing left retroperitoneal mass with central vascularity. Subsequent abdominal MRI detailed the mass as large with lobulated margins and central cystic changes, plus metastases to left abdominal para-aortic lymph node, multiple lung nodules in lower lobes bilaterally, and liver nodules, indicating neoplastic disease. Bone scan revealed no bone metastases. Biopsy with immunohistochemistry showed tumor cells negative for markers including LCA, WT-1, DESMIN, Myogenin, phox-B2, CD99, SOX10, Chromogranin, and GATA3, but positive for CK, FLI-1, and Synaptophysin. The pathology report concluded compatibility with renal PNET/Ewing sarcoma, confirming diagnosis. No documented bone metastases were found. The clinical course and treatment details were unavailable from the source evidence.
